'''Brady Thomas West''' is an American [[statistician]], academic and author. He is a research professor in the Survey Methodology Program (SMP) at the Survey Research Center (SRC) in the Institute for Social Research (ISR), and a research professor in the Department of Biostatistics within the School of Public Health,<ref name=rdx>{{Cite web|url=https://surveydatascience.isr.umich.edu/west|title=Brady T. West &#124; Michigan Program in Survey and Data Science|website=surveydatascience.isr.umich.edu}}</ref> both at the [[University of Michigan]], Ann Arbor. He also serves as an Adjunct Research Professor in the Joint Program in Survey Methodology (JPSM) at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]]<ref name=car>{{cite web|url=https://jpsm.umd.edu/landingtopic/our-faculty|title=Our Faculty - Joint Program in Survey Methodology}}</ref> and as an Adjunct Instructor at the Odum Institute for Research in Social Science at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://odum.unc.edu/event/issues-in-the-analysis-of-complex-sample-survey-data/|title=Issues in the Analysis of Complex Sample Survey Data|website=The Odum Institute - UNC Chapel Hill}}</ref>

West is most known for his research on measurement error, survey estimation, [[selection bias]], survey design, [[interviewer effect]]s, and [[Multilevel model|multilevel regression models]]. He is the lead author of a book titled ''Linear Mixed Models: A Practical Guide using Statistical Software'', ''Third Edition'', which compares different statistical software packages in terms of their [[Mixed model|mixed-effects modeling]] procedures, and is also the co-author of ''Applied Survey Data Analysis'', among other books.<ref name="riv">{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1751-5823.2010.00122_17.x|title=Applied Survey Data Analysis by Steven G. Heeringa, Brady T. West, Patricia A. Berglund|first=Martin|last=Crowder|date=December 18, 2010|journal=International Statistical Review|volume=78|issue=3|pages=463|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1111/j.1751-5823.2010.00122_17.x|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

West was elected [[List of fellows of the American Statistical Association|Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/|title=American Statistical Association|website=American Statistical Association}}</ref> As of 2024, he serves as an associate editor of ''[[Journal of Survey Statistics and Methodology]]''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/jssam/pages/Editorial_Board|title=Editorial Board|website=Oxford Academic}}</ref> and [[Sociological Methods & Research]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/SMR|title=Editorial board}}</ref> and an editorial board member of ''[[Field Methods]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/FMX|title=Editorial Board: Field Methods: Sage Journals}}</ref>

==Education and early career==
West earned a B.S. in [[Statistics]] from the University of Michigan (UM), Ann Arbor, in 2001, followed by a M.A. in Applied Statistics from the same university in 2002. He worked as a Computer Systems Consultant II and Senior Statistician/Statistical Consultant in the Center for Statistical Consultation and Research at UM during 2003 to 2007. He was appointed as a Statistician Lead for Consulting for Statistics, Computing, and Analytics Research (CSCAR) at UM from 2007 until 2018. During this time, from 2008 to 2011, he worked as a Graduate Student Research Assistant at the SMP in the ISR. He also served as an Associate at Daves and Associates Research from 2010 to 2012 while earning a Ph.D. in [[Survey Methodology]] from UM in 2011.<ref name=rdx/>

==Career==
From 2011 to 2016, West served as a research assistant professor at the University of Michigan and an adjunct research assistant professor at the University of Maryland-College Park, and held the position of research associate professor and adjunct research associate professor from 2016 to 2022, respectively. He has been a research professor in the Department of Biostatistics within the School of Public Health at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, since 2023, and a research professor in the SMP at the SRC in the ISR since 2022.<ref name=rdx/> Additionally, he has served as an adjunct instructor at the Odum Institute for Research in Social Science at the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill since 2012, and as an adjunct research professor in the JPSM at the University of Maryland-College Park since 2022.<ref name=car/>

West has held numerous professional appointments throughout his career. In 2016, he was elected as associate chair of the education committee on the [[American Association for Public Opinion Research|AAPOR]] executive council, assuming the role of chair for the subsequent term spanning 2017 to 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aapor.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/2_Minutes_July_6.pdf|title=AAPOR Executive Council Meeting}}</ref> and as the council's associate chair of the conference committee in 2021, ultimately serving as chair of the 2023 AAPOR annual conference.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.www-archive.aapor.org/About-Us/Leadership/Committees-and-Taskforces.aspx?cid=EXEC-COUNCIL|title=Committees and Taskforces - AAPOR}}</ref>

==Research==
West's research has explored measurement error in auxiliary variables, survey [[paradata]], selection bias, responsive survey design, [[interviewer effect]]s, and multilevel regression models for clustered and longitudinal data.<ref name=rdx/> His work has been featured in media outlets such as ''[[The New York Times]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/01/04/sports/ncaafootball/04score.html|title=In B.C.S., Dollars Are the Only Relevant Numbers|first=Nicholas|last=Bakalar|date=January 3, 2009|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref> ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'',<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/how-uncle-sam-conducts-surveys-1461334374|title=How Uncle Sam Conducts Surveys|first=Jo Craven|last=McGinty|newspaper=WSJ }}</ref> and ''[[The Michigan Daily]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/research/this-is-not-ok-umich-research-finds-increased-reports-of-forced-intercourse-in-us-during-pandemic/|title=UMich research finds forced intercourses increased during COVID|first=Ji Hoon|last=Choi|date=September 20, 2023|website=The Michigan Daily}}</ref>

West's publications have contributed to survey methodology and research. He is the lead author of the third edition of ''Linear Mixed Models'', which focused on comparing mixed-effects modeling methods across different software. Carlos A. Coelho called its first edition "A very good starting point for those willing to get a more in-depth knowledge of LMMs",<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/15598608.2012.695708|title=Linear Mixed Models: A Practical Guide Using Statistical Software by Brady T. West, Kathleen B. Welch, and Andrzej T. Galecki: Chapmann & Hall/CRC Press (2006)|first1=Carlos A.|last1=Coelho|first2=Abel M.|last2=Rodrigues|date=September 18, 2012|journal=Journal of Statistical Theory and Practice|volume=6|issue=3|pages=590–595|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1080/15598608.2012.695708|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and Petra Macaskill applauded the authors "for undertaking—and to a large extent succeeding in—such an ambitious project."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://public.websites.umich.edu/errors/404.html|title=U-M Web Hosting|website=public.websites.umich.edu}}</ref> Toral Burghoff recommended the second edition book even to owners of the first edition, noting its coverage of various situations where LMMs are applied and its demonstration of commonly used software packages in different settings.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/bimj.201500240|title=Linear-Mixed Models—A Practical Guide Using Statistical Software, Second Edition . B. T.West, K. B.Welch, and A. T.Galecki. (2015). Boca Raton, FL: Taylor and Francis/CRC Press. 440 pages, {{text|ISBN-10:}} 1466560991, {{text|ISBN-13:}} 978–1466560994|first=Toral|last=Burghoff|date=May 18, 2016|journal=Biometrical Journal|volume=58|issue=3|pages=717–718|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1002/bimj.201500240|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Likewise, Andreas Ziegler, a book review editor of ''Biometrical Journal'', praised the third edition, stating, "This book is perfect for readers seeking a quick reference for various situations where LMMs are applicable."<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/bimj.202300025|title=Linear mixed models. A practical guide using statistical software by Brady T.West, Kathleen B.Welch, Andrzej T.Gałecki, third edition, New York: Chapman & Hall/CRC. 2022. 489 pages. {{text|ISBN:}} 978-1-0031-8106-4. List price: £ 84.99|first=Andreas|last=Ziegler|date=April 18, 2023|journal=Biometrical Journal|volume=65|issue=4|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1002/bimj.202300025|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2010, West co-authored the book, ''Applied Survey Data Analysis,'' presenting a statistical overview of how to correctly apply modern techniques for design-based analysis of complex sample survey data. The book is in its second edition. Martin Crowder wrote that "…there is a wealth of instruction here. The writing style is expansive, keeping mathematics in check, and the material is well organized clearly into appropriate sections. I think that the book would serve any budding survey practitioner well."<ref name="riv"/>

West also served as a co-editor of the 2017 volume ''Total Survey Error in Practice'', which offered insights into [[total survey error]] (TSE) and provided tools to enhance survey data quality amidst evolving large-scale datasets, emphasizing efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. In collaboration with Annelies G. Blom, he presented a research synthesis analyzing the impact of human interviewers on survey processes, using the TSE framework to assess historical trends, identify knowledge gaps, and shape future research on interviewer effects.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/jssam/article-abstract/5/2/175/2452318|title=Explaining Interviewer Effects: A Research Synthesis}}</ref> Afterward, in 2019, he co-edited the book ''Experimental Methods in Survey Research'' that delved into the experimental designs within surveys, incorporating both probability and non-probability samples, while employing a TSE perspective to illuminate the strengths and limitations of these techniques across various disciplines. Katherine Jenny Thompson, in her review of this work, said, "As an overview of quantitative research applied to survey methodology, the book is a success. The variety of topics is comprehensive, and the literature overviews are generally very informative."<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Book Review: Paul J. Lavrakes, Michael W. Traugott, Courtney Kennedy, Allyson L. Holbrook, Edith D. de Leeuw, and Brady West. Experimental Methods in Survey Research: Techniques that Combine Random Sampling with Random Assignment . 2019, Wiley, {{text|ISBN:}} 978-1-119-08374-0, 544 pages|first=Katherine Jenny|last=Thompson|date=December 1, 2020|journal=Journal of Official Statistics|volume=36|issue=4|pages=941–943|doi=10.2478/jos-2020-0046|doi-access=free}}</ref> Additionally, he co-edited ''Interviewer Effects from a Total Survey Error Perspective,'' published in 2020, examining interviewer roles, challenges, and solutions within [[survey data collection]], with a focus on training, management, analysis, and data quality optimization through the TSE framework. ''A [[Public Opinion Quarterly]]'' review called this book "a timely contribution to the literature on survey interviewing," highlighting its holistic approach in studying interviewers, survey processes, and errors for a complete understanding."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/poq/article-abstract/85/1/242/6207653|title=Kristen Olson, Jolene D. Smyth, Jennifer Dykema, Allyson L. Holbrook, Frauke Kreuter, and Brady T. West, eds. Interviewer Effects from a Total Survey Error Perspective }}</ref>

===Public health and medicine===
West's applied research has examined substance use, mental health, and discrimination among diverse U.S. populations, revealing heightened risks for certain sexual orientation groups,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Sexual orientation, substance use behaviors and substance dependence in the United States|first1=Sean Esteban|last1=McCabe|first2=Tonda L.|last2=Hughes|first3=Wendy B.|last3=Bostwick|first4=Brady T.|last4=West|first5=Carol J.|last5=Boyd|date=August 18, 2009|journal=Addiction|volume=104|issue=8|pages=1333–1345|doi=10.1111/j.1360-0443.2009.02596.x|pmid=19438839|pmc=2975030}}</ref> increased odds of substance use disorders for LGBT adults experiencing discrimination,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=The Relationship Between Discrimination and Substance Use Disorders Among Lesbian, Gay, and Bisexual Adults in the United States|first1=Sean Esteban|last1=McCabe|first2=Wendy B.|last2=Bostwick|first3=Tonda L.|last3=Hughes|first4=Brady T.|last4=West|first5=Carol J.|last5=Boyd|date=October 18, 2010|journal=American Journal of Public Health|volume=100|issue=10|pages=1946–1952|doi=10.2105/AJPH.2009.163147|pmid=20075317 |pmc=2937001 }}</ref> and complex relationships between sexual orientation, race/ethnicity, and gender with mental health disorders.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Discrimination and mental health among lesbian, gay, and bisexual adults in the United States.|first1=Wendy B.|last1=Bostwick|first2=Carol J.|last2=Boyd|first3=Tonda L.|last3=Hughes|first4=Brady T.|last4=West|first5=Sean Esteban|last5=McCabe|date=March 18, 2014|journal=American Journal of Orthopsychiatry|volume=84|issue=1|pages=35–45|doi=10.1037/h0098851|pmid=24826824|pmc=4144327}}</ref> He has also highlighted disparities in depression care utilization across ethnic and racial groups,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1001/archgenpsychiatry.2009.168|title=Depression Care in the United States: Too Little for Too Few|first1=Hector M.|last1=González|first2=William A.|last2=Vega|first3=David R.|last3=Williams|first4=Wassim|last4=Tarraf|first5=Brady T.|last5=West|first6=Harold W.|last6=Neighbors|date=January 1, 2010|journal=Archives of General Psychiatry|volume=67|issue=1|pages=37–46|via=Silverchair|doi=10.1001/archgenpsychiatry.2009.168|pmid=20048221 |pmc=2887749 }}</ref> and elevated substance use disorder risks among sexual minorities due to childhood victimization.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Victimization and substance use disorders in a national sample of heterosexual and sexual minority women and men|first1=Tonda|last1=Hughes|first2=Sean Esteban|last2=McCabe|first3=Sharon C.|last3=Wilsnack|first4=Brady T.|last4=West|first5=Carol J.|last5=Boyd|date=December 18, 2010|journal=Addiction|volume=105|issue=12|pages=2130–2140|doi=10.1111/j.1360-0443.2010.03088.x|pmid=20840174|pmc=3006226}}</ref>

West has also made contributions to studies focusing on [[prescription drug]] use and abuse in the United States. In particular, his work has brought to light the importance of prevention efforts targeting children and adolescents,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Does early onset of non-medical use of prescription drugs predict subsequent prescription drug abuse and dependence? Results from a national study|first1=Sean E.|last1=McCabe|first2=Brady T.|last2=West|first3=Michele|last3=Morales|first4=James A.|last4=Cranford|first5=Carol J.|last5=Boyd|date=November 30, 2007|journal=Addiction|volume=102|issue=12|pages=1920–1930|doi=10.1111/j.1360-0443.2007.02015.x|pmid=17916222|pmc=2377405}}</ref> the crucial role of continued monitoring in guiding prevention and intervention efforts,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Trends in medical use, diversion, and nonmedical use of prescription medications among college students from 2003 to 2013: Connecting the dots|first1=Sean Esteban|last1=McCabe|first2=Brady T.|last2=West|first3=Christian J.|last3=Teter|first4=Carol J.|last4=Boyd|date=July 1, 2014|journal=Addictive Behaviors|volume=39|issue=7|pages=1176–1182|doi=10.1016/j.addbeh.2014.03.008|pmid=24727278 |pmc=4349373 }}</ref> the need for enhanced vigilance in prescribing and monitoring opioids among adolescents,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Leftover Prescription Opioids and Nonmedical Use Among High School Seniors: A Multi-Cohort National Study|first1=Sean Esteban|last1=McCabe|first2=Brady T.|last2=West|first3=Carol J.|last3=Boyd|date=April 1, 2013|journal=Journal of Adolescent Health|volume=52|issue=4|pages=480–485|doi=10.1016/j.jadohealth.2012.08.007|pmid=23298996 |pmc=3608842 }}</ref> and national trends in medical and nonmedical use of prescription opioids among US high school seniors.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2016-2387|title=Trends in Medical and Nonmedical Use of Prescription Opioids Among US Adolescents: 1976–2015|first1=Sean Esteban|last1=McCabe|first2=Brady T.|last2=West|first3=Phil|last3=Veliz|first4=Vita V.|last4=McCabe|first5=Sarah A.|last5=Stoddard|first6=Carol J.|last6=Boyd|date=April 1, 2017|journal=Pediatrics|volume=139|issue=4|pages=e20162387|via=Silverchair|doi=10.1542/peds.2016-2387|pmid=28320868 |pmc=5369669 }}</ref>

Within the context of medical research, West's work has identified cholestasis and age-adjusted small bowel length as major predictors of mortality in pediatric short bowel syndrome, along with the presence of the ileocecal valve for successful weaning from parenteral nutrition.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Pediatric Short Bowel Syndrome|first1=Ariel U.|last1=Spencer|first2=Andreea|last2=Neaga|first3=Brady|last3=West|first4=Jared|last4=Safran|first5=Pamela|last5=Brown|first6=Imad|last6=Btaiche|first7=Barbara|last7=Kuzma-O'Reilly|first8=Daniel H.|last8=Teitelbaum|date=September 18, 2005|journal=Annals of Surgery|volume=242|issue=3|pages=403–412|doi=10.1097/01.sla.0000179647.24046.03|pmid=16135926|pmc=1357748}}</ref> In related research, he was involved in a study that underscored improved survival rates with the ipilimumab-radiotherapy combination in melanoma brain metastases, highlighting the significance of multimodality therapy for achieving better outcomes.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Ipilimumab and radiation therapy for melanoma brain metastases|first1=Ann W.|last1=Silk|first2=Michael F.|last2=Bassetti|first3=Brady T.|last3=West|first4=Christina I.|last4=Tsien|first5=Christopher D.|last5=Lao|date=December 18, 2013|journal=Cancer Medicine|volume=2|issue=6|pages=899–906|doi=10.1002/cam4.140|doi-access=free|pmid=24403263|pmc=3892394}}</ref>

==Personal life==
West is married to Laura Elizabeth West, with whom he has two children: Carter and Everleigh. He lives in [[Dexter, Michigan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://surveydatascience.isr.umich.edu/west|title=Brady West}}</ref> He is the son of Kenneth and Tommi West, of Livonia, Michigan,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://turowskifuneralhome.com/obituaries/norma-mozier.112318|title=Obituary Norma Mozier}}</ref> and has a brother, Daniel West, who is the director of crisis services for the Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network in Detroit, Michigan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dwihn.org/board-PCC-August2022-agenda.pdf|title=Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network - Daniel West}}</ref>
